question.text: A Cat III AIF's 'Risk Management Framework' should include:

answer.text: An independent risk/compliance function, material risk reporting, liquidity management, prudential leverage controls, counterparty/concentration/leverage risk review, and VaR as a risk metric

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (pages 66, 123-126, 208-210, 225-226 and 260) describes a comprehensive risk management framework with independent risk management and compliance functions when leverage is deployed, material risk reporting, liquidity management for redemptions, prudential/leverage controls, review of concentration/counterparty/liquidity/leverage risk, and VaR as a risk metric. The Trap: Single-factor approaches (only VaR, only daily PnL, only year-end audit) are inadequate to manage the multi-dimensional risks of a Cat III AIF. Note: The independence of the risk and compliance functions is particularly important when the fund deploys leverage.
